rules.statement: A plaintiff can assert a servitude of drawing water from a well even if their land is separated by a public road or intervening land, provided the intervening land has a similar servitude.
rules.supporting_quote: "For which reason it became the custom that water could lawfully be led by right of servitude through the adjoining estates of more than one person, and that one and the same servitudes of passage, driving, and way, could be constituted over several farms of several owners; and the right of drawing water was not stopped by the fact that there existed an intervening public road or place."
